title: Terumah: gold inside and out (Exodus 25:11)
hook: the ark is gilded inside and out; the Talmud says a scholar's inside must match his outside (Yoma 72b)
tomorrow: Terumah: the cherubim face each other (Exodus 25:20–22)

segments.voice: Yesterday, in Terumah: make me a sanctuary, that I may dwell among them. Your line was among them, not in it. Did you find a small space for quiet? Today, the first object in the plans: the ark. Day three hundred fifty-five.

Every kitchen has a drawer like this. The front of it is lovely: painted wood, a brass handle. Pull it open and it's chaos. Rubber bands, dead batteries, a key nobody can identify. People can be a bit like that drawer. A polished outside, a different story inside. Most of us have been both the drawer and the person surprised by one. The first thing the Torah describes in the sanctuary plans isn't a wall or an altar. It's a box: the ark that will hold the tablets of the covenant. And the instructions for gilding it are oddly specific about the inside.
screen: `A LOVELY DRAWER, CHAOS INSIDE.` → `THE FIRST OBJECT: A BOX.` → `GILDED WHERE NO ONE LOOKS.`

segments.voice: The ark is made of acacia wood, two and a half cubits long, about four feet. Then the instruction, in the old Jewish translation: "within and without shalt thou overlay it." Gold on the outside, which people might glimpse. Gold on the inside, which almost no one would ever see. The tablets would sit in there, and the ark would stand in the holiest room, where only the high priest entered, once a year. So why gild the inside? The Talmud gives a picture. Betzalel, the craftsman, made three boxes, it says: a gold one, a wooden one, and another gold one. The wooden box sat inside the outer gold, and the inner gold sat inside the wood. Gold, wood, gold. And then Rava, a great sage of Babylonia, draws the lesson. Any scholar, he says, whose inside is not like his outside is not a true scholar. In Hebrew that's tocho k'baro, his inside like his outside. The Talmud remembers a head of the academy, Rabban Gamliel, who once wouldn't let a student into the study hall unless his inside matched his outside. Notice the ark isn't solid gold. There's wood in the middle: ordinary, living material. Nobody is asked to be pure metal all the way through. The ask is simpler, and harder. Be the same inside as you appear outside. Don't polish only the side people see.
screen: `WITHIN AND WITHOUT SHALT THOU OVERLAY IT.` · `GOLD, WOOD, GOLD: THREE BOXES.` · `TOCHO K'BARO: INSIDE LIKE OUTSIDE.` · `WOOD IN THE MIDDLE.` · then, large: `GOLD INSIDE AND OUT.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: check the inside of the box. Settle, and breathe. Think of one place where your outside and inside don't match right now. Maybe you seem calm at work and you're frayed underneath. Maybe you act generous and feel resentful. Maybe you say you're fine. Don't judge it. Just notice the gap, honestly. Then ask: what's one small step toward matching? Telling one person the truth. Letting the outside soften. Or doing the inside work no one will see. The bell holds the time.
Terumah. Our portion, where the ark is overlaid with gold inside and out, and the Talmud says a scholar's inside must match the outside.
Your line: gold inside and out. Today, do one good thing that nobody will see, and let your inside match your outside. Day three hundred fifty-five.

howItsDone: Tocho k'baro, inside like outside, is a common phrase in Jewish ethical teaching about integrity, and the ark's gold within and without is often cited for it in sermons on Terumah.

fork.reveal: within and without shalt thou overlay it. the Talmud pictures gold, wood, gold, and draws the lesson: inside like outside.

original.note: Hebrew: his inside like his outside; the Talmud's phrase for integrity.

trapdoor: what you thought: a fancy gold box.
what it means: gold where no one looks; the inside matters as much as the outside.
what a scholar hears: Yoma 72b: Betzalel made three arks, gold, wood, gold; Rava: a scholar whose inside isn't like his outside is no scholar.

notes: Exodus 25:11 phrase quoted from JPS 1917 from memory (KJV identical for these words); verify.
Two and a half cubits ≈ 3.75 feet; 'about four feet' given. Confirm.
Yoma 72b: three arks (Betzalel made three arks); Rava's teaching on tocho k'baro. Confirm attribution (some cite it in the name of Rava, others note the parallel).
Berakhot 28a: Rabban Gamliel's rule barring students whose 'inside is not like his outside'. Confirm.
The tablets in the ark and the high priest's yearly entry on Yom Kippur are standard; confirm phrasing.
